DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dil . ov. h OILG OPINION NO. APR 28 2025 HELEN D. SALVADOR Sangguniang Bayan (SB) Secretary Office of the Sangguniang Bayan Municipality of Gen. Mariano Alvarez Province of Cavite Dear SB Sec. Salvador: This has reference to your Letter dated January 20, 2025 addressed to Engr. Danilo A. Nobleza, CESE, Provincial Director of DILG Cavite, requesting this Department's opinion regarding designation of the Municipal Tricycle Franchising and Regulatory Board (MTFRB) Chairperson of the Municipality of Gen. Mariano Alvarez (GMA), Cavite. As represented, a letter was sent by Hon. Maricel E. Torres, Municipal Mayor of GMA, to the Sangguniang Bayan, respectfully requesting to be designated as the Chairperson of the MTFRB to ensure better oversight and for thorough verification of franchising documents. Specifically, you asked the following: 1. "Whether the designation of the Mayor as the MTFRB Chairperson is mandated or discretionary, and if so, what legal framework or issuance this is established? 2. Any precedents, issuances or related legal doctrines supporting such a designation. 3. The potential legal and operational implications of alternative designations. " Considering that the issues are interrelated, we deem it prudent to discuss the same in one discussion. The enactment of the Local Government Code (LGC) of 19911 brought about significant reforms in the implementation of land transportation laws by the Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC), now the Department of Transportation (DOTr), more particularly the franchising and regulatory functions being exercised by the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) with respect to the operations of tricycles-for-hire. Republic Act No. 7160. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

As stated in Land Transportation Offico (L TO) v. City of Butuan2. the power of the DOTC, through the LTFRB, to grant franchises and to regulate the operations of tricycles-for-hire has now been devolved to the local government units (LGUs). Such devolution is due to the fact that the LGUs are in a better position to address the concerns of tricycle drivers operating within their respective city or municipality, Relevant to the query of Ms. Salvador aro tho following pertinent provisions under the LGC regarding the powers, duties. and functions of tho Municipal Mayor, to wit. "SEC. 444. The Chief Executive: Powers, Duties, Functions, and Compensation. — xxx (b) For efficient, effective, and economical governance the purpose of which is the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code, the municipal mayor shall: (I) Exercise general supervision and control over all programs, projects, services, and activities of the municipal government, and in this connection, shall: (i) Determine the guidelines of municipal policies and be responsible to the sangguniang bayan for the program of government." On the other hand, the LGC explicitly states the power of the Sangguniang Bayan to grant franchises and to regulate the operations of tricycles-for-hire. Sec. 447, paragraph (3)(vi) of the LGC provides: "SEC. 447. Powers, Duties, Functions, and Compensation. — xxx (3) Subject to the provisions of Book II of this Code, grant franchises, enact ordinances authorizing the issuance of permits or licenses, or enact ordinances levying taxes, fees, and charges upon such conditions and for such purposes intended to promote the general welfare of the inhabitants of the municipality, and pursuant to this legislative authority shall: xxx (vi) Subject to the guidelines prescribed by the DOTC, regulate the operation of tricycles and grant franchises for the operation thereof within the territorial jurisdiction of the municipality." 2 G.R. No. 131512, January 20, 2000 Page 2 of 4

Based on the foregoing, there is no specific provision under the LGC which mandates the Municipal Mayor to be the Chairperson of the MTFRB, nor any prohibition on designating him/her in such position, While the Municipal Mayor is not expressly prohibited from holding the position of Chairperson, the LGC is clear that the franchising and regulatory power shall be exercised by the Sangguniang Bayan. The use of the word "shall" in a statute means that it is mandatory.3 As such, pursuant to Sec. 447, paragraph (3) of the LGC in relation to paragraph (vi) thereof, it is settled that the power to regulate the operation of tricycles and to grant its franchise were conferred unto the municipal government, specifically the Sangguniang Bayan. It is also noteworthy to mention that under the LGC, the power of the Sangguniang Bayan to regulate and grant franchise is still subject to the guidelines prescribed by the DOTC. In lieu of the LTFRB, among the powers devolved to the Sangguniang Bayan is the power to "issue, amend, revise, renew, suspend or cancel Motorized Tricycle Operator's Permit (MTOP) and prescribe the appropriate terms and conditions therefor."4 Thus, the issuance of the M TOP or the document granting franchise or license which allows a natural or juridical person to operate tricycle-for-hire5 falls under the authority of the Sangguniang Bayan. Primarily, the composition of the MTFRB, its powers and functions, and the qualifications of its members will be stated in the ordinance to be enacted by the Sangguniang Bayan. Likewise, the procedure for the grant, denial or revocation of the tricycle franchise, the documents required for the application, and other terms and conditions thereof will be set forth in the same ordinance. Nonetheless, since the LGC does not prohibit the Municipal Mayor from acting as the Chairperson of the local franchising and regulatory board, the Sangguniang Bayan, as the legislative body of the municipality, can exercise its sound discretion and designate the former as Chairperson of the MTFRB, also through an ordinance. Pursuant to Sec. 444, paragraph (b)(l) of the LGC, the Municipal Mayor, as the local chief executive, may oversee the processing of tricycle franchise in the exercise of its general supervision and control over all programs, policies, and projects of the municipal government, provided that it is in accordance with the ordinance and subject to the limitations under the LGC and court decisions. 3 Power Sector Assets and Liabilities Management Corporation v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue, G.R. No. 198146, August 8, 2017. 4 Guidelines to Implement the Devolution of LTFRB's Franchising Authority Over Tricycles-for-Hire to Local Government Units Pursuant to the Local Government Code (R.A. No. 7160). Ibid. Page 3 of 4

All things considered, please note that this opinion is based solely on the facts disclosed in the letter and the issues raised therein. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of the courts and competent authorities. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: A . ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPBtLLLS-LRALLD/nab cc: ARIEL O.
